Name: Spooky Scary Interface
Author: Doragoun
Description:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/sCrfQoK.png[/img]
Spooky scary skeletons...

[img]https://media.tenor.com/uDCPw_UdZOoAAAAC/skeleton-dance.gif[/img]﻿

aren't what you're going to find here. Still, welcome! Made for the Stardew Valley Discord server's mod jam, this Halloween-themed purple and orange UI might just be the perfect thing to get you in the right spooky mood.
In addition to the color scheme, prepare yourself for spider webs, bats and a jack-o'-lantern as the friendship indicator.

One thing to note here: Due to the mostly magenta backgrounds, the default shadow for the font might look slightly out of place. While it's not gamebreaking, it makes things harder to read – because of that, you might want to install a mod that removes these shadows. I personally used [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/12467]Font Settings[/url] for taking the screenshots, but [url=https://m.blog.naver.com/khs3400/222049471897]Fix Font Option[/url] from the Korean site Naver also works well.

The UI should work properly for all language versions and support both PC and Android. If you find something looking strange that's not recolored properly or have any other feedback or comments, please let me know!


[img]https://i.imgur.com/chykWEd.png[/img]﻿
After you've launched the game with this mod installed once, a config.json containing all your settings will be generated inside its mod folder. Changing that file manually (which I definitely don't recommend) or preferably using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]GMCM[/url] allows you to edit these settings. The available configs are...
[list]
[*][b][b]Spooky Season[/b]:[/b] Determines when the UI will be active – defaults to all year round like other UI mods, but you can also configure it to be used only in fall or only on Spirit's Eve. This way, you can use other UIs for the rest of the year and make fall appropriately spooky.
[*][b]Dialogue Box Style[/b]: Allows you to choose from four different styles for the exterior of the dialogue box – either an all-new border with rounded corners or the good old wooden border. Both styles come in purple and orange – check the mod images to see what they look like.
[*][b]Cursors[/b]: Allows you to turn the edits to the in-game cursors on and off. If you want to use another mod to edit them, set the changes from this mod to false.
[/list]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/sgtIh0y.png[/img]﻿
Easy! Make sure you've got Content Patcher installed, then download this mod and unzip it into your mods folder – that's it.
To uninstall, simply delete the folder again.


[img]https://i.imgur.com/e1dXF3S.png[/img]﻿
Should be compatible with just about everything!

This UI is made to load after most (hopefully all?) popular UI mods. This means that, if you set the Spooky Season config to fall or Spirit's Eve, you'll be able to use other UI mods that are replaced by this UI only in fall or on Spirit's Eve. If there's a UI that doesn't play nicely, you'll need to add a so-called false dependency to this mod's manifest.json. [url=https://stardewmodding.wiki.gg/wiki/Tutorial:_How_to_Add_a_False_Dependency_for_Load_Orders]This page[/url] has more information on the process, but I already prepared a "template" in the dependencies section – simply add your UI mod's unique ID (found in its own manifest) and remove the slashes. If you need help, don't hesitate to leave a comment, though. :)

Additionally, there are some specific compatibility patches for popular mods that add UI elements included in the main download. By replacing the original assets with the recolored ones, nothing should stand out as vanilla-colored next to all the orange and purple. If there's something you think should definitely have its own patch, please let me know and I just might make one!
